briefing.text: Sector attention data is for 2026-11-16. On News, Information Technology stayed #1 (buzz 86.0, up 3.6 on the day, down 1.7 on the week, mentions up 305%, sentiment -0.1) led by NVDA, MSFT, AMD, INTC and AVGO. Financials was the big riser, jumping from #11 to #2 (buzz 85.2, up 20.3 on the day and 9.5 on the week, mentions up 126%, sentiment 0.01) on BAC, UBS, MS, JPM and C. Real Estate (buzz up 7.8, mentions up 239%) and Materials (buzz up 6.2, mentions up 337%) also gained. On X, Information Technology stayed #1 (buzz 93.3, flat) with NVDA, MU and AMD, Financials moved from #4 to #2 (buzz 91.1; HOOD, SOFI, JPM, BAC), and Utilities mentions fell 80%. On Reddit, Information Technology stayed #1 (buzz 94.2, sentiment -0.04) on NVDA, INTC and AAPL, while Utilities (buzz up 11.9, mentions up 123%) and Financial Services (buzz up 13.8, mentions up 145%) rose and Healthcare buzz fell 11.9.

KLAR #1: Klarna launched an AI shopping assistant and reported strong Q3 results, 16 positive vs 3 negative articles; it reports earnings today, so the news helps explain the rank.
TTWO #2: Headlines say the stock keeps falling ahead of the GTA VI release (-4.5% on the day, -10.1% over 5 days); the news matches the heavy X attention.
HD #3: Earnings analysis pieces are out (147 articles in 2 days, mixed tone); it reports today, so the news explains the rank.
LOW #4: Top headlines are about Palo Alto and TJX earnings, not Lowe's; its own earnings are 11-18, so the rank rests more on X attention than on its own news.
DIS #5: Earnings coverage is strong (Morningstar says strength persists across Experiences and Streaming; 53 positive vs 6 negative); this explains the rank.
JPM #6: Headlines are about an Apple-linked outage that locked people out of bank accounts and flights, a broad story rather than JPM-specific; it adds to the heavy news volume (639 articles).
WMT #7: Investor's Business Daily says it is nearing a buy point before earnings on 11-19, and Target earnings are in the news; this explains part of the rank.
UAL #9: The same outage story (blocked boarding flights) and 38 negative vs 6 positive articles, with a 4% drop on the day; the news fits the attention spike.

Klarna ranks first (score 0.928) because attention is 0.79 above normal and X attention 0.975 above normal, both near the top of the field, volume is 2.17 above normal, and it reports earnings today. Take-Two is second (0.925) on attention 1.12 and X attention 1.16 above normal with 190 X mentions, despite weak volume (0.61) and a 10% 5-day drop ahead of GTA VI. Home Depot is third (0.922) with the highest X attention reading in the set (1.31 above normal, top percentile) and attention 1.15 above normal, plus an earnings catalyst today; its volume (0.61) and momentum (1.06 sigmas) are middling. Attention and X attention carry 35% of the weight each, which is why these three lead.

notes: Ranks are by the scoring of record (pick_rank, w2). Prices and moves as of the last pull of the day. Facts from public data; not investment advice.
